aiOverview.content: The Information and Communications Technology Authority (ICTA) manages procurement for the World Bank-financed Kenya Digital Economy Acceleration Project (KDEAP) (Project ID: P170941), a US$390 million initiative running through 2028. aiOverview.content: The Communications Authority of Kenya (CA) launched a public consultation in September 2026 proposing a standalone colocation data centre licence to replace the previous Network Facilities Provider Tier 2 (NFP-T2) classification.Standalone Licence Proposal: Shifted data centres out of general telecom infrastructure classes to offer lower initial fees and tailored rules on resilience, physical access, and service continuity.Power Constraints & Stalled Projects: Major large-scale projects, such as the proposed Microsoft and G42 $1 billion geothermal data center in Olkaria, faced delays over government payment guarantees and power-capacity limits (with 1GW demands creating grid-balancing challenges).Active Infrastructure Growth: Established players like iXAfrica (hosting Oracle's cloud region in Nairobi), Africa Data Centres, and iColo continue expanding capacity as Kenya's market tracks toward an estimated USD 800+ million valuation by 2031.Active Tenders & RFPs: Public sector and institutional bids (such as equipment supply, server integration, and cloud expansion advisory like Konza Cloud) are tracked via procurement platforms like KenyaTenders and TendersOnTime.If you are looking for a specific RFP document, procurement code, or closing deadline from a particular Kenyan government agency or private operator (such as Konza, KenGen, or Safaricom), please share the name or sector so I can pull the exact details.If you are looking for a specific RFP document, procurement code, or closing deadline from a particular Kenyan government agency or private operator (such as Konza, KenGen, or Safaricom), please share the name or sector so I can pull the exact details.
